newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls regulation imposing duties on Opel Austria.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls regulation imposing duties on Opel Austria.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance annulled on Wednesday a regulation passed by the Council of the European Communities which had the effect of withdrawing tariff concessions granted to Opel Austria.

The European Econonic Area agreement concluded with Austria was approved in December, 1993, seven days before the Council adopted the contested regulation imposing a 4.9 percent duty on F-15 gearboxes originating in Austria and exported to the Community.

Opel Austria, a wholly owned subsidiary of General Motors, USA, argued that the adoption of that regulaton flew in the face of the EEA agreement which prohibited tariffs between Austria and the Community.

The court agreed and annulled the contested regulation stating that once the EU has adopted an international agreement and the date of entry into force is known, traders may rely on the principle of protection of legitimate expectation to challenge contradictory measures adopted by EU institutions.

Case T-115/94
Opel Austria, applicant
supported by
Republic of Austria, intervener
v
Council of the European Union, defendant
supported by Commission of the European Communities, intervener

application to annul Council regulation (EC) No 3697/93 of 20 December 1993, withdrawing tariff concessions in accordance with the Free Trade Agreement between the Community and Austria (OJ 1993 L 343, p. 1)
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby

1. Annuls Council regulation (EC) No 3697/93 of 20 December 1993 withdrawing tariff concessions in accordance with article 23(2) and article 27(3)(a) of the Free Trade Agreement between the Community and Austria (General Motors Austria);
2. Orders the Council to bear its own costs and pay the applicant's costs;
3. Orders the Commission and the Republic of Austria to bear their own costs.
